notesStmt.note: The corrections on this manuscript were not incorporated into the version of the poem that appeared in Harper's, November Boughs, or the deathbed edition of Leaves of Grass, but they were most likely made between late 1884 and 1888. Whitman was in the habit of ordering batches of specially printed poem slips that he then "corrected" in small ways and presented as mementos to friends and admirers. However, while several other similar proof slips are extant, none of them contain these same corrections, which suggests this slip was not intended for that purpose.
A corrected proof slip of the poem "Of That Blithe Throat of Thine," which was first published in Harper's Monthly Magazine in January 1885. The poem was later included in November Boughs (1888).

lg.head: Of that Blithe Throat of Thine.

epigraph.p: [More than 83 degrees°83/s north—about a good day's steaming distance to the Pole by one of our fast oceaners in clear water—Greely heard the song of a single snow-ϑbird merrily sounding over the desolation.]

lg.l: Of that blithe throat of thine from arctic bleak and blank,

I'll mind the lesson, solitary bird—let me too welcome chilling
drifts,

E'en the profoundest chill, as now—a torpid pulse, a brain un-
nerv'dunnerv'd
Old age land-lock'd within its winter bay—(cold, cold, O cold!)
These snowy hairs, my feeble arm, my frozen feet,
For them thy faith, thy rule I take, and grave it to the last;

Not summer's zones alone—not chants of youth, or sourth's warm
tides alone,

But held by sluggish floes, pack'd in the northern ice, the cumulus
of years,
These with gay heart I also sing.
